name: Pasupatheeswarar Temple, Tirukkondeeswaram
deity: Shiva as Pasupatheeswarar (Jurahareswarar), with the goddess Shanthanayaki
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Tirukkondeeswaram, on the southern bank of the Mudikondan near Nannilam, honours Shiva as Pasupatheeswarar with the goddess Shanthanayaki. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Appar, it is bound to Kamadhenu's worship — from which the lord is Pasupateeswarar — and to sage Agastya, whose fever Shiva cured here, so that he is also Jurahareswarar.

sections.history: Tirukkondeeswaram lies about 17 km north of Tiruvarur, on the southern bank of the Mudikondan river, with Nannilam (another Paadal Petra Sthalam) about 2.5 km to the west, in Tiruvarur district. Listed in the Tevaram as Tirukkondeechuram, it is a Paadal Petra Sthalam whose hymns are attributed to Appar (Tirunavukkarasar). The area was once a forest of bilva trees, Vilvaranyam; the stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Pasupatheeswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Shanthanayaki in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. The lingam is said to bear the mark of a cow's horn, from the sthala legend. The temple keeps the form of the Shiva shrines of the Nannilam delta.
sections.legends: In the sthala purana, Parvati was cursed to take the form of Kamadhenu, the celestial cow; her horns struck the buried lingam, and she poured her milk over it to staunch the hurt — a scar from the horn is said to be visible still. Because the divine cow (pasu) worshipped here, Shiva is Pasupateeswarar, 'the lord of cattle.' When sage Agastya came with a high fever, the lord cured it unasked, and so is also called Jurahareswarar, 'remover of fever.' The goddess Shanthanayaki stands beside him.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims on the Nannilam stretch of the Paadal Petra temples include Tirukkondeeswaram among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tirukkondeeswaram the pilgrim comes to the lord of cattle by the Mudikondan. Before Pasupatheeswarar and Shanthanayaki, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple of the Nannilam delta, and the memory of Kamadhenu's worship and the fever Shiva turned aside for Agastya.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirukkondeeswaram lies about 17 km north of Tiruvarur, on the southern bank of the Mudikondan, with Nannilam about 2.5 km west, in Tiruvarur district. Nannilam and Tiruvarur are the nearest towns and rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
